records.t: Chapter 17 Facet separability Fanning out to a focused judge per construct asserts, on faith, that those constructs are separable. This chapter is the certification under that assertion: whether a decomposition is a real topology, one axis wearing two names, or a prerequisite dressed as a peer.

Correlation is symmetric. It can say two facets move together; it cannot say that breaking A degrades B while breaking B leaves A intact. That asymmetry is the whole question, and it is invisible to any correlation-shaped measure, the orthogonality audit included. So the audit intervenes. Over a joint-state panel, events labelled by which facets' defects were injected, it reads each direction separately: how much facet F's score moves when F's own defect is injected, against how much it moves when G's is. Verdict Signature What it means What to do separable Both ratios low Independent axes. Keep both. collinear-collapse Both high, symmetric One axis wearing two names. Rejoin. This is the only verdict where rejoining is right. asymmetric-subsumption One high, one low The high-ratio facet subsumes the low one: a prerequisite or constituent relationship, not a duplicate. Keep both. The subsumed one is the sharp sub-dimension; the other is the catch-all. unverified Undersampled, a dead own-axis, or a compensatory coupling Not established. Nothing yet. Reported rather than rounded to separable. The trap this closes A saturation or collinearity signal on its own says "these look redundant, rejoin them." That is right for collinear-collapse and wrong for asymmetric-subsumption , where rejoining destroys a real, independently manipulable axis. Collinear behavior is a hypothesis. Run the factorial before you rejoin.

Two things depend on the answer being right. A fan-out is a claim about topology. Minting three focused judges per subject asserts those three constructs can be judged apart. If two of them are one axis, you have bought two judges' latency and cost for one axis of signal, and their agreement will read as corroboration when it is tautology. Reflection depends on it further downstream. Full orthogonality is one of the grant's hard preconditions, and a decomposition that has not certified cannot satisfy it. See What has to hold before a cell reflects .
Three reads, in order of cost. The screen proposes a hypothesis, the audit certifies it, the monitor re-checks it cheaply.

POST /lens/redundancy/screen { "surfaceId": "classify-intent" } Over per-event score vectors it returns the pairwise collinearity matrix and, for each collinear pair, two things the matrix alone does not give: a scrap-pick naming which twin is the dependent copy, and a residual localization naming the substrate column that holds the copy's only independent variance. Omit dimensionIds and every scored dimension on the surface is screened. Data-gated. A pair below the minimum sample floor reads undersampled and a dimension with no variance reads no-variance , with a pointer at the saturation audit, since a dimension that never moves is usually a blind judge rather than a redundant one. The screen withholds rather than fires on a thin panel.

POST /lens/facet-topology/audit { "surfaceId": "classify-intent", "facets": [ { "dimensionId": "hrv-provenance", "defectColumn": "defect.hrv", "defectValue": "injected" }, { "dimensionId": "place-identity", "defectColumn": "defect.place", "defectValue": "injected" } ] } Each facets entry is a panel-based expectation: the facet's score dimension, the diagnostic substrate column marking its injected defect, and the value that marks the defect as present. At least two are required, because the question is about a pair. provenance defaults to all , so a replay or emitted panel is in scope, and correlationIdPrefix scopes to one. options takes the cell-size floor and the ratio cutoffs where a surface needs them; the defaults are conservative. Read-only, so propose-only. The audit returns a verdict per unordered pair and the operator promotes the split, keeps it, or rejoins. The audit inherits its panel's validity A facet whose own injected defect does not move its own score reads as a fake subsumption. Those pairs are reported as such rather than scored. The audit is only as good as the ablation underneath it: if the defect you injected was not a defect, nothing downstream of it is a measurement.

POST /lens/pairwise-monitor/run { "surfaceId": "classify-intent" } The audit is expensive and offline. The monitor is the cheap online guard on it. Over per-event defect co-firing it returns, per dimension pair, the co-trigger counts and a phi coupling adjusted for how often each dimension fires on its own, which is what separates real coupling from a shared score floor, plus the signal for a pair collapsing toward collinear while live. Give it the characterized band as expectedBands and it returns a drift verdict proposing a re-run of the audit. Run the audit with persist: true and it closes the loop itself: the audit also runs the monitor over the same window and appends a durable characterization record merging the verdict with the co-trigger band per pair, which is what the monitor reads back. bandTolerance sets the band's half-width, 0.1 by default. The monitor proposes drift. It never adjusts a band, because a band that moves itself measures nothing.

records.h: When the judge and the producer disagree
records.t: POST /lens/contested-cohort/screen { "surfaceId": "classify-intent", "dimensionId": "correctness" } The adjacent question, converging on the same fields. For one judged dimension it partitions events by each candidate substrate-column cohort and tests whether the judge's fail-rate on a cohort value is elevated against the rest of the population, with the family under false-discovery control. A contested cohort is one where the producer's outputs are systematically rejected. It is reported with the producer's own within-cohort consistency alongside, because a producer that is consistently doing one thing and consistently marked down for it has a different shape from one that is erratic. The lens cannot adjudicate which party is right, and does not try. It points at the interaction, notes that a focused judge on that field would isolate it, and routes to review. Cohorts below the sample floor are withheld.

Every read here is read-only and propose-only, and three of the attention spine's sources file from them: redundancy-candidate , which mints a rejoin-dimension proposal, plus pairwise-drift and contested-cohort , which mint nothing. A source with no default proposal is one where the remedy is a judgment the lens leaves to the operator. All four are data-gated and report honest nulls. A withheld pair, an undersampled cohort and an unverified verdict are all distinguishable from a clean result, which is the property that makes a quiet report worth anything.

Method & path Purpose POST /lens/redundancy/screen The collinearity matrix, with a scrap-pick and residual localization per collinear pair. POST /lens/facet-topology/audit The interventional audit. Returns a verdict per unordered pair; persist: true also records the characterization and its band. POST /lens/pairwise-monitor/run The online guard: co-trigger counts, the adjusted phi coupling, and a drift verdict against the characterized band. POST /lens/contested-cohort/screen Cohorts where the judge systematically rejects the producer, with the producer's within-cohort consistency.

Upstream is Rubric coverage and de-saturation : a de-saturation fan-out creates the facets this chapter certifies, so the two run as one loop rather than two tools. Alongside it at axis altitude is the orthogonality audit in Variance isolation , which asks whether a declared substrate column explains anything, a different object measured a different way. The audit procedure, the coupling measure and the tuning constants ship inside the binary. The verdict vocabulary and the record shapes are public contract.

records.h: When the judge and the producer disagree

records.t: Chapter 18 Judge modes and reflection Every judge/gate relationship on a surface is one of four modes, the valid cells of two independent questions: does the producer wait for the verdict, and may the verdict touch delivery. Reflection is the third cell, and the only one Holonograph grants rather than leaving to configuration.

Two axes. Timing is async (the judge runs off the producer's hot path) or inline (the producer waits for the verdict before finishing). Authority over delivery runs open (observe only) to reflection (the judge may send the producer back to retry) to gate (delivery is blocked). open reflection gate async Open, asynchronous impossible impossible inline Open, inline Reflection granted Actually gated The two empty cells are impossible rather than unspecified. Reflection and gating both need the verdict before the producer finishes, and an asynchronous verdict is not back yet. The consequence is worth stating plainly: async is available only to a judge that observes and nothing more.

Across all four modes the judge's authority stops at reflection. It can observe, and at most it can send the producer back to try again. It cannot block delivery. Disposal belongs to deterministic code in the gate, which is producer-owned, or to operator policy. Propose-only holds in every mode.

records.h: Inline and observing is the expensive cell
records.t: A judge that runs in-request while its verdict touches nothing pays full latency for no in-band effect. A fleet of observe-only judges parked there is where large latency overheads come from. The cell is justified as a step toward reflection or a gate, not as a destination. Move the judge to async, or give it authority.

Pick the mode per surface. A judge that only records belongs in async. Reflection is a capped retry, not a block. Budget the retries. A gate is deterministic code reading a verdict. Write the gate; do not ask the model to be one.

An asynchronous verdict lands after the producer has answered, as a linked judge event. A reader resolves it link-first and falls back to the embedded verdict, fail-open, so a consumer never blocks on a verdict that has not arrived. Per-judgment verdict provenance distinguishes the raw judge result from the producer-filtered one.

Reflection turns a judge from an evaluator you read into an optimization target the producer chases. That inverts the trust requirement. A judge you only read can be a little wrong, because you flag and a human reviews. A judge you optimize against has to be right, because the producer will find and exploit every gap in it. The gate is on validity, not on discrimination. Those come apart: a judge can score stably and still be blind, saturated, or wrong about how a construct should treat absence. Scoring the same way every time is reliability, and reliability does not imply validity.

Real dimensions are often requires-confirmation: an honest "I do not have the data" correctly scores low. Put that judge in a retry loop and the cheapest way for the producer to raise its score is to stop being honest about the absence and fabricate. That is the exact failure the apparatus exists to catch, now with a loop optimizing toward it. So reflection without established authority is not merely a waste of tokens and time. It is a pressure applied to the one behavior you most need preserved.

records.h: What has to hold before a cell reflects
records.t: Reflection unlocks for a judge × rubric × facet × surface cell when all of the following hold. The gate is dual: Holonograph computes the statistical pass, then a human confirms. Soak. Enough live production data to reach a statistical N. Holonograph determines the statistical pass; a human approves the N, judging whether the sample spans the breadth of real inputs and outputs. Discrimination. The facet's dimensions pass discrimination evaluation, with a human confirming key outlier calls and a statistical sampling of calls on that facet. Saturation cleared. Every dimension passes the saturation audit, which is a read you can run yourself . Validity is cell-specific, so the grant is too. A judge certified on one facet of one surface has said nothing about another.

A failing response returns to the producer with the judge's grounded critique attached, and the producer retries, capped. Reflection is the soft tier of the judge's authority over delivery: it can send the producer back, it cannot block. Blocking remains deterministic code in the gate, or operator policy.

The grant is revoked on any change to the identity it was computed on. A new judge model, a revised rubric, a changed context scope: the cell certifies again or it does not reflect. This is the authority machinery applied to the judge rather than to the producer, and it suspends the same way for the same reasons.

One of those preconditions has an instrument of its own. Groundedness has to hold on both sides: a judge that read a different frame from the producer is not measuring the producer, and a groundedness alarm on such a pair points at the wrong party. POST /lens/co-groundedness/screen { "surfaceId": "classify-intent" } Over the surface's claim-instrumented judged dimensions it classifies each judge-to-subject frame relation: Relation What it says shared-frame-intact Judge and producer were grounded in the same values. A groundedness finding here is about the producer. judge-misread-frame The judge read the frame wrong. The finding is about the judge. judge-frame-truncated The judge saw part of the frame. Its verdict is scoped to what it saw, whatever it asserts. judge-grounded-outside-frame The judge grounded on something the producer never had. It is marking the producer down for an absence that was never the producer's. not-assessable The relation could not be established. Reported rather than assumed intact. The last two are the observer-groundedness asymmetry, and they are the disambiguation to run before treating a groundedness alarm as a producer fault. Deterministic per verdict, certain or abstain: no false-discovery gate and no data floor, because each relation is established or it is not. Read-only, so it proposes and the operator disposes.

Method & path Purpose POST /lens/co-groundedness/screen Classify the judge-to-subject frame relation per claim-instrumented dimension. Your own reflection loop remains yours to run; nothing here prevents it. The claim is narrower: a retry loop against an uncertified judge spends tokens to apply pressure in an unknown direction. Holonograph turns reflection on when the cell has qualified, if you have asked for it. The taxonomy is the design of record for the judge/gate relationship and is documented ahead of the implementation. The reflection path and the judge-gate enforcement cluster each have their own specification; this chapter is the frame that places them.

Chapter 19 Seams A value whose meaning is not fixed by its representation, driving a decision that governs a consequential transition, is a seam. It is permanent. You can close it and you can monitor it. You cannot validate it away.

A seam is an edge: the path a value travels from where it is produced to the decision that consumes it. Write it I → DP , interpretive source to decision point. Whether an input is interpreted is a property of that edge, not of the field and not of whether the code is deterministic. The same field can lie on a deterministic edge to one consumer and an interpreted edge to another. A model output, a classifier, an approximate match, a pattern applied to free text, an external feed, a recorded human judgment: each is an interpreted source, and each is interpreted because of what the consuming decision does with it. The decision point reverts to an ordinary, inert sink under one condition only: it stops making decisions. Its output goes to a log line, a rendered field, a return nobody branches on. Short of that, the seam stays.

Consider a decision that reads free text and returns one of three values: function decide(ticket): 'page' | 'auto-reply' | 'queue' { const msg = (ticket.subject + ticket.body).toLowerCase(); // I0 if (INCIDENT.test(msg)) return 'page'; ... } const action = decide(ticket); // I1: deterministic in value, interpreted in provenance if (action === 'page') pageOnCall(); // dispatch on I1 reaches authority The enum is not a sanitizer. It is the decision's codomain. action is a first-class interpretive value, deterministic in what it holds and interpreted in where it came from. The chain runs I0 → DP → I1 → DP1 and onward, and the provenance rides through every hop. Relocating the decision upstream moves the decision point; it does not escape anything. The next scan finds it in its new place.

records.h: Validation changes the character of the error, not its existence
records.t: A schema boundary filters the catastrophic: wrong type, missing field, malformed JSON. It passes the shape-valid-but-wrong. So it raises the floor and, in the same motion, makes the residual error insidious, because the value now looks right, types right, and fails without a signal downstream. A pattern that pulls 'success' out of "I hope you are a great success in life" and resolves it to route.SUCCESS is the whole problem in one line. The enum fixed the form, not the misread. It is a confidently wrong signal wearing a valid badge. This is why structure cannot finish the job. Closing a seam makes the decision attended and monitorable. It does not make the decision correct. Correctness is a different axis, the empirical misfire rate, and the only instrument for it is soak. Structure hands off exactly the error class it cannot catch to the instrument that can.

With provenance carried, the two states have a precise inductive definition over the chain. State Condition closed The decision point is attended, meaning it has a defined no-match or abstention path, and its output's provenance chain terminates in non-deciding sinks. Every downstream consumer is either another closed decision point or something that does not decide. open Any unattended decision point in the chain, or a chain that feeds an unattended authority decision point. The defective state. A closed seam is a declared surface. It stays closed only while its measurement holds, which is why closed and ready for soak belong in the same breath.

These are the structural forms a closure takes. They are shapes, not an exhaustive list of the decisions that can exercise authority; the sink taxonomy is an open registry. Shape Form regex-over-value A pattern tested, matched or replaced against the interpreted value. branch-on-value An if or switch comparing the value to literals. threshold-on-value An if comparing the value to a numeric literal. value-as-key The value used as an index or map key.

A model call is a seam whose interpreter is not stationary. A pattern does not rewrite itself between releases; a model can be re-routed behind an unchanged alias, and the instrument scoring it is usually another model. So a model seam carries more variance machinery: the four-source decomposition, the served-model axis, judge facets, saturation and orthogonality. The machinery differs; the lifecycle does not. Code seams and model seams both soak, both file findings on the spine, and both reach authority. They sit on adjacent surfaces, not in separate systems. A seam is itself a light source, recorded as seam/<component>/<scan> , which is how a non-model interpreter takes the same slot a vendor would without being recorded as one.

The shape is the lens's own judge → verdict → gate → action model applied inside ordinary code: decide → enum → dispatch → sink is the same structure. The enum is a verdict, carrying light from an interpreted source, and a dispatch acting on it is governed by that light.

records.t: Chapter 20 The seam monitor The monitor has a build-time half and a run-time half over one record. Source analysis produces evidence, a gate adjudicates it, a confirmed seam is registered as a surface, and soak measures whether the closure holds against real inputs.

Five stages, each with one job and one output. The separation matters: the scanner is an evidence producer, not an adjudicator. Stage Role Output Source scan Evidence producer A candidate interpretation edge, as structural facts Interpretation gate Semantic adjudication A typed disposition Registration Declaration A surface on the append-only record Run-time producer Viability measurement Soak findings on live traffic Authority state Consumer The per-surface reading over all of the above The scan reports what it can establish structurally: that a value originates from a known source locus, flows through named identifiers, reaches a branch, threshold, pattern or key sink, and that the default path has a particular shape. It never emits a verdict.

The gate answers one question before the authority machine asks any of its own: is this a closure over an open interpreted domain at all? Disposition Meaning certain-interpreted The input's meaning is not fixed by its representation and the edge governs authority. A real seam; the state machine applies. certain-mechanical The edge is deterministic or the domain is closed. An exact match, an enum lookup. Not a seam. unresolved Abstain. The apparatus cannot yet tell, so it withholds the disposition and keeps measuring. Only certain-interpreted edges become registered records. Abstention here means withholding a consequential disposition and continuing to measure. It is not a queue of requests for a human.

records.h: The scanner is its own dark surface
records.t: Finding seams is itself a closure over an open domain, namely arbitrary code, so it reports its own blind spots as first-class coverage rather than as silence. coverage.status : the overall coverage state for the scanned unit. coverage.supported_constructs : the language constructs the front end actually handles. coverage.unresolved_edges : edges the taint could not fully follow. coverage.unparsed : code the front end could not parse. coverage.dynamic_escape : points where dynamic dispatch, reflection or serialization broke the path. Partial coverage is never reported as no seams. A scan that could not follow an edge says so, and the hook that reports into a build session says so too rather than issuing a false all-clear.

The monitor flags and drafts. It does not edit code and it does not block on the lens's own authority. Whether a build stops is a policy the operator or CI sets, and the detector must qualify before that policy is even eligible: observe first, everywhere, including the detector run against its own repository. The criterion that governs that qualification is the one the invariant demands of every other instrument. Under rising uncertainty the detector must abstain more, not assert more.

Scan a repository and push its seams to the lens, or run the hook so a seam is reported into the session that wrote it. --propose-sinks and --propose-skips mechanically propose candidates for the authority-sink and skip-path lists rather than asking you to author them cold. Accepted declarations are honored: a seam you declare drops from the lens as well as from the scan. Each reported seam names the authority sink it reaches, so the choice is to declare it or restructure around it.

A soak is the empirical life of a registered seam: how often its no-match or abstention path actually fires, which branch it takes, how the decided value's identity churns over time, and optionally whether that value is efficacious. A soak observation is a full evaluation event rather than a new event kind, so every existing tool works on it unchanged: the producers, the dashboard, retention and husking, the judge link. The seam-ness lives on the run-time configuration axes instead. Axis Value provenance seam . The isolation key. It sits in neither the production-state nor the exploratory-state set, so soaks are excluded from every default analysis and cannot drown a small agent's readings. runMode The shared enum. Isolation is provenance-keyed and independent of run mode, so eval and replay mean here what they mean everywhere. lightSourceIdentifier seam/<component>/<scan> . A seam is a light source that is not a model, and it takes the slot under its own name rather than a vendor's. The husk-surviving facts, whether it abstained and which path it took and the value fingerprint, ride in the surface dimension, the substrate columns and the cohort tags. A raw decided value rides in the payload and husks away like a judge rationale.

The scan and the soak are the first two layers of one instrument. Both sit above a question neither answers: when a call went wrong, which seam on its path was involved? Layer Where it runs The claim it can make Definition The scanner, over source This seam could influence that call. Observation The lens, at its own boundary This call happened, and this is what crossed the boundary. Analysis The lens, over the observations This seam's appearance is associated with failure, confound-controlled. The lens trusts only what it observes at its own boundary One invariant discharges two constraints at once. Nothing is added to your code, because the evidence is the mediated traffic the lens already sees. And the subject’s own account is never evidence: a seam's resolved arm counts only when it was recovered from the request and response bytes. An arm the builder asserts has its own grade, self-reported , which exists so the lens can refuse it rather than fold it silently into observed evidence.

records.h: Why a linkage stays a candidate
records.t: Joining a call to a candidate seam through the call site proves the call site executed. It does not prove the seam took part. Every linkage from that join is graded static-only , including when the call itself was observed, and a deterministic join never promotes a candidate to observed . Only independent boundary evidence does, such as an arm value recovered injectively from the call's own bytes. A call-site frame that resolves to no node in the scan is unknown . Because every linkage is a candidate, this read is monitor-only evidence and deliberately does not feed the attention queue. A separability signal that filed as a finding would be an attribution claim the evidence does not support. GET /lens/seam-call-observations?surfaceId=classify-intent Re-derived per read from the stored call events joined against the candidate map, with nothing stored as an observation and no new event kind. Honest-empty until call sites are captured and a map is pushed, never a 501 : a read with no candidates is an answer.

GET /lens/seam-call-analysis?since=2026-10-01T00:00:00Z Over those observations: the judge fail-rate on calls where a seam node appears against the rest of the panel, per node, with the family under false-discovery control. A row reads the seam as a whole or conditions on one resolved arm. Each association is then conditioned on a confound, the model, the version or the input cohort, and carries the verdict: robust where it survives within the strata, sampling-confound where it collapses once the confound is held constant, insufficient where the stratified cells are too thin to say. The last is reported rather than rounded to robust. Alongside the associations: each seam's structural reach, its arm distribution, and the pre-registered pools of related nodes. Every number is a separability signal, never a causal claim.

Soaks file under one reserved surface, adjacent to the surface registered seams file under, with individual seams as loci inside it. Findings from both reach the attention spine as builder-seam and seam-soak sources, alongside every other finding the instrument produces. An abstention observed at the boundary is a first-class value rather than an absence, so a surfaced no-match path is distinguishable from an arm the lens could not see. An arm that never manifests in mediated traffic is unknown , paired with a null resolved arm, and stays that way.

Method & path Purpose POST /lens/builder-seams The scanner pushes its current registered-seam set. Replace-current: a scan run is a complete re-derivation of the code's interpreted seams, so the newest push is the truth and a seam that no longer appears is gone. Writes the evidence registry only, never the contract registry. Returns 202 { accepted } once the write is durable and visible to other instances. 501 where the registry is not wired, which is the only opt-in. GET /lens/builder-seams Confirm an ingest landed and is visible cross-instance before its call events start carrying a call-site id. A per-source summary by default; ?full=1 returns the held scans. GET /lens/seam-call-observations The re-derived seam-to-call linkages, each graded observed , static-only or unknown . Monitor-only evidence; never a finding. Takes surfaceId , since , until . GET /lens/seam-call-analysis Confound-controlled failure associations per seam node, with structural reach, arm distribution, related-node pools and the false-discovery summary. Caveats carry the honest nulls. POST /lens/seam-soak/judge Run the offline value-efficacy judge over a seam's stored raw-output corpus. Operator-invoked, approver and cost gated. The judge runs over the stored corpus, never the live stream, and verdicts are minted server-side on the judge surface. 501 where no judge scorer is wired. The shared vocabulary, the four sink shapes, the default-path forms and the sink kinds, lives in the public contract package so the build-time scanner and the run-time producer name the same things. The interpretation disposition is the same enum the authority state machine reads.
