records.t: Chapter 21 The attention spine Every observe-only surface produces findings, and there are twenty-six sources of them. The spine gives all of them one operator lifecycle instead of one list per surface, and it is the substrate the authority state reads.

A cross-source triage layer over findings. It declares three objects and nothing else: Object What it holds FindingRef The stable identity of a finding, independent of the scan that produced it. TriageRecord An append-only annotation about that finding. Proposal What a confirmed finding mints into Curate.

Twenty-six, spanning judge behavior, evaluation structure, coverage, attribution, the store, and the seam work. They are listed here because the spine is only as good as what files into it. Group Sources Judge behavior verdict-reliability , judge-liveness , judge-malfunction , co-groundedness Evaluation structure orthogonality-hypothesis , primary-axis-orthogonality , redundancy-candidate , pairwise-drift , contested-cohort , rubric-gap , rubric-ref-broken Coverage and reach coverage-gap , reach-gap , emission-gap , dark-mass-blindspot , read-window-underpowered Surface lifecycle and attribution trajectory , quarantine-candidate , retirement-candidate , hash-provenance , source-conflation Seams and authority builder-seam , seam-soak , authority-suspended Store store-capacity , retention-integrity A code seam and a model call file into the same spine. They arrive from different sources and sit on adjacent surfaces, and from the lifecycle's side they are the same object.

When several of a swarm's agents emit onto one surface, pooling them is sometimes right and sometimes fabricates a statistic. Every source declares which, so a new producer cannot pool two agents by omission. Partition Behavior per-source Pooling corrupts the statistic or destroys attribution, so the source runs once per agent and each finding is stamped with its sourceId . A no-op where one surface has one agent. The analytic reads over scores and variance sit here: pooling two score populations manufactures correlation that neither agent shows. pooled-examine Pooling is correct, because the instrument is shared, the contract is global, or the grouping is the operator's and not the lens's to override. The source-conflation alarm checks these for a hidden per-agent split and surfaces it without imposing a partition. pooled Global, or keyed on a different axis entirely: the consumer's agent id, the rubric, the lens's own store. A per-agent split is not meaningful and the alarm ignores it. source-conflation is the twenty-sixth source and the one that reads the others: it compares agents inside a pooled read and reports where a single number is hiding two populations. It points, it does not repartition. Whether an operator's grouping is wrong is the operator's call.
What a finding's identity means depends on its grain: run for one call, conversation for one conversation, and structural for a declared surface, dimension or axis with no single event behind it.
Two invariants hold the spine apart from the measurement it annotates.

records.h: A triage annotation never reaches the substrate
records.t: An annotation is about a derived finding. It lives in a separate store, downstream of derivation. It is never an input to the lens hash, and it never mutates the substrate, a prompt, or a threshold. The spine proposes; the existing gated approver path disposes. A triage click changes nothing on the lens.

Findings are re-derived on every scan. A triage record therefore keys to a content-derived findingKey rather than a per-scan row index. Keying to a row index would orphan every annotation on the next deploy. clusterId stays an attribute, never the primary grain, because a non-deterministic key has the same effect.

Read findings from the spine rather than per-surface. One queue, one lifecycle. Annotate a finding to record what triage concluded. Annotations accumulate; nothing is overwritten. Mint a proposal from a confirmed finding. The proposal enters the approver path as a proposal, not as a change.

GET /lens/attention?surfaceId=classify-intent&state=untriaged&severity=alarm&limit=50 Authorization: Bearer <token> x-holonograph-run-mode: production Filters: surfaceId , source , state , severity , sort , since , until , limit , cursor . Severity is one of alarm , needs-review or coverage , which is the ranking the default sort uses. Each item carries findingRef and its derived findingKey , the source , the severity , a count of the events that collapsed into it, firstSeen and lastSeen , the inline evidence , the derived triageState , the latestTriage record, how , and gate . The queue reads without a triage store Without a triage store wired, the queue still returns: every finding reads as untriaged. Writes are what need the store, and POST /lens/attention/triage answers 501 without one. An unconfigured deployment loses the lifecycle, not the observability.

GET /lens/attention/evidence?findingKey=<key> The decision-grade detail behind one row, fetched when an operator opens it rather than for every row in the queue. It returns a representative exemplar , the most recent flagged call in the class, with the prompt, the model's answer, the judge's verdict and rationale, and the mechanical claims: the tool the judge said was not invoked, the datum it said was fabricated. Alongside it, sampleCount and a samples list to spot-check, plus reAdjudicable and unavailable . Re-derived per read; nothing is persisted. A class that no longer recurs in the window returns an honest-null exemplar rather than a stale one.

POST /lens/attention/triage Authorization: Bearer <token> Content-Type: application/json { "findingRef": { "primary": { "grain": "structural", "id": "..." }, "attributes": { ... } }, "disposition": "confirmed-defect", "rationale": "the judge passed three misuse samples in a row", "approverId": "brian" } rationale and approverId are required: an annotation without a reason or an author is not a compliance record. Two optional fields pin what the operator saw, evidenceSnapshotRef for the denormalized slice and asOf for the substrate instant, so a decision stays reconstructible after the evidence moves on. The server stamps occurredAt itself.

A disposition is what the operator wrote. A state is what the queue derives. Value Kind Meaning confirmed-defect disposition Adjudicated real. This is the one that mints a proposal. false-alarm disposition Adjudicated not real. acknowledged disposition Real and accepted: a known blind spot the operator chooses to leave. Parked, not dismissed. untriaged state only No record yet. resolved state only The proposal was applied through Curate, or the finding stopped recurring. A lifecycle signal sets it, never a triage click.

Twelve authoring targets. Each lands in Curate approver-gated, carrying intent rather than an apply-payload: the operator authors the change. Proposal kind Default source The remedy grounding-cap-bump verdict-reliability Raise the grounding cap the flagged verdicts are hitting. gate-dimension judge-liveness Put a dimension under a gate. adjust-threshold operator-raised Move a passThreshold . predicate-downweight trajectory Downweight a trajectory predicate that over-fires. declare-axis orthogonality-hypothesis Declare an emitted-but-undeclared column as its own axis. Splits a confound out. rejoin-dimension redundancy-candidate Collapse a dependent dimension into the twin it duplicates. The inverse of declare-axis : this merges a copy back into the axis it never left. retire-surface coverage-gap , retirement-candidate Retire a surface, or mark it forward-declared. release-from-quarantine quarantine-candidate Release a quarantined stream. author-rubric rubric-gap Author a bespoke per-facet rubric for a facet that has only ridden the default. fix-rubric-ref rubric-ref-broken Repair a rubric reference that no longer resolves. author-fixture operator-raised Author a fixture the surface is missing. retention-policy store-capacity , read-window-underpowered Adopt or tighten a retention preset. The operator sets the policy; the lens never compacts on its own. Fourteen of the twenty-six sources mint nothing by default, source-conflation among them. A source with no default proposal is not a lesser finding: it is one where the remedy is a judgment the lens leaves to the operator.

A finding carries its findingRef , the surface and dimension it came from, the run mode it was derived under, and its triage state. Where a finding has an exemplar, the exemplar payload travels with it under the same husk projection used elsewhere in the store, so a triaged finding on a compacted span still opens.

The spine is the base. Authority is a reading over the same record: a per-surface state derived from what the gates, the dependencies and the soak evidence say, re-derived on every read. A surface whose grant is withdrawn files authority-suspended back onto the spine as another finding, which is how a withdrawal reaches the same queue as everything else. Reflection sits above that again, switched on for a cell once its authority is established.

Method & path Purpose GET /lens/attention The cross-source queue: findings merged with triage state, severity-ranked, cursor-paginated. GET /lens/attention/evidence The exemplar and sample list behind one finding. POST /lens/attention/triage Append one annotation. 501 without a triage store. GET /lens/trajectory-findings The trajectory source read on its own: the turn-to-conversation axis a per-turn judge structurally cannot see. Groups events by the consumer's boundary column, runs the detectors, and returns the findings alongside the honest-null accounting (events with no boundary key, turns with no output text, which predicates actually ran) so an unmeasured slice never reads as clean. All three are also served under the /holonograph alias. The reads derive per request and persist nothing; the write touches the triage store only, which is not an input to the lens hash. The public module declares the wire and store contract only. Which surface maps to which FindingRef , and the store implementation, live in the lens package.

Chapter 22 Authority Authority is a state held per decision surface: the declared prerequisites for a specified consequential transition are satisfied on the record as it stands. It is established only by the satisfaction of the gates its contract names, it is re-derived at every read, and no actor confers it.

Four neighbouring words get used for this and none of them is it. Term What it means Permission An actor is allowed to act. Approval An actor affirmatively accepts something. Correctness A proposition matches an applicable reference. Confidence A degree of belief, or a measurement's precision. Authority The declared prerequisites for this transition are satisfied on the record. Humans, builders and mechanicals all produce events on the record. No kind of actor confers authority. An operator approving a decision is approval, recorded as such; it does not move the state.

An ordered ladder a decision surface climbs, plus the one state the apparatus can drop it into. State Meaning unmapped No authority sink has been identified here. The honest default: not yet mapped, rather than no seam. mapped A sink is identified, but nothing asserts authority over it. The seam exists; no claim of certainty stands on it. declared Authority is asserted and the gate is live, but the certainty condition is not established and no qualifying evidence is accruing. qualifying Asserted and actively accumulating the evidence that would establish the condition. Live traffic is exercising the sink. granted The declared certainty condition is established on live evidence and every dependency holds. suspended Authority was granted and a dependency left its declared condition, so the apparatus withdrew the grant itself. Default ordering puts suspended first, because a grant withdrawn out from under a live decision is the loudest thing on the page. granted and unmapped are the quietest: one is working as intended, the other is a coverage note rather than an alarm.

A reading is computed from the recorded events at every read. No state is stored, so a reading cannot drift from the substrate it describes. A reading also never mutates anything: the apparatus proposes, the operator and CI dispose.

records.h: The authority stack and its conditions
records.t: Every object whose identity or value a grant was computed on is recorded as a stamped column. The set of them is the surface's authority stack. Where a dependency is a model, the recorded identity is the one that served the call, not the one requested. Each dependency declares the envelope within which a change leaves the grant valid. Condition Envelope identity The default. The dependency must be the same thing. equivalence A different thing, declared equivalent. reach Within a declared reach. band Within a declared band. A change inside the envelope is recorded and raised for review, with no transition. A change outside it suspends. Re-establishing a withdrawn grant takes the re-satisfaction of every gate over the post-change record, not an acknowledgement.

A tear is a served or judge model value appearing on a surface for the first time. The soak window anchors at the previous stack change, held back to the segment before the latest unacknowledged tear, and a tear never self-clears . An operator acknowledgement releases it; the window then starts no earlier than the acknowledged tear, and the acknowledgement leaves an append-only, server-minted audit record that is never compacted. Releasing a tear, and setting what one release covers, are the operator's two standing dispositions over authority. Both are gated and both leave a record. See Authority governance .

Declare the surface and its contract: what the decision concludes, on what evidence, under what prerequisites, with which abstention path and gate composition. Let it run. A surface without traffic cannot accumulate the evidence that would qualify it, which is why declared and qualifying are different states. Read the map rather than a single number. A living system holds authority on every surface rarely and briefly; which surfaces hold it, and what withdrew the rest, is the reading.

Method & path Purpose GET /lens/authority One reading per gated dimension, plus an honest unmapped reading for every gate-less surface. Re-derived per read. The five governance routes, the tears read and the policy desk among them, are in the next chapter .

Each entry carries surfaceId and dimensionId , the state , the interpretation that identifies the sink, the contract and its preconditions , the statistical power , any accuracyHold or reSoak , the suspension when there is one, and the basis the state was derived from. A reading is always present, so an absent surface cannot pass for a healthy one. The state ontology, the dependency-condition kinds, the stack and contract shapes and the pure state machine are public contract. Signal extraction, turning gate composition, floors, versions and drift into the preconditions the machine maps to a state, lives in the lens.

Chapter 23 Authority governance Authority is a reading the lens derives and never writes. Two dispositions over it belong to the operator: releasing the hold a tear puts on a surface’s soak window, and setting what one release covers. Both are gated, both are attributed to a named operator, and both leave a record the compactor will not touch.
Three parts: the gate every privileged write passes through, the acknowledgement that releases a tear, and the standing policy that says what an acknowledgement covers.

Every privileged write on the lens carries an approverId and is refused without one. A self-asserted id that disagrees with the verified operator on the request is refused too, so the stamped identity is not the caller’s claim about itself. Who may act is a separate question, and the lens does not answer it. Tier policy lives in the operator’s identity system, so authorization is a pluggable resolver, absent by default. With none wired, any identified operator may proceed and the action is stamped with their id. Wire one and the same endpoints enforce its decision, denying with 403 . The lens records who acts before it constrains who may act. The resolver is asked about one action at a time, and the action vocabulary is deliberately fine-grained, so an identity system can grant the cheap dispositions widely and the expensive ones narrowly. Action Gates multiplex.run A live, billable cross-vendor fan-out. subscriptions.write Standing config that fires outbound webhooks. retention.compact Executing one reviewed compaction plan, or undoing an archive seal. retention.policy The standing retention disposition, which can compact unattended. authority.acknowledge-tear Releasing the soak-window anchor one tear holds. authority.policy Changing what an acknowledgement covers. archive.rehydrate Mounting a read-only overlay of archived payload. data.erase An irreversible erasure about a data subject. seam.judge Running the offline value-efficacy judge, which spends money. Two of the nine are authority’s, and they are separate on purpose. More people can reasonably be trusted to release one tear than to change how every future release is recorded.

A tear is a served or judge model value appearing on a gated surface for the first time. The surface’s authority soak window anchors at the previous stack change, held back to the segment before the latest unacknowledged tear, and a tear never self-clears. So a tear is not a notification. Releasing it moves the window forward, which can let a torn surface re-qualify and let its pre-tear span be summarised. That is a disposition over authority, which is why it has a gate of its own and an audit record rather than a dismiss button.

The authority reading is only worth what its evidence window is worth. A window that slid forward over a model change on its own would be reporting one instrument’s record as another’s, and nothing downstream could tell. Holding the window and making an operator say, on the record, that the span is still one subject is the property that keeps the reading meaningful. The mode that governs those releases is a standing disposition, not a per-call choice. Under the default, one acknowledgement covers every earlier open tear on the surface. Under per-tear , each tear takes its own, oldest first. An identity system can only express the distinction between releasing a tear and changing that mode if the two are separate actions.

GET /lens/authority/tears?surfaceId=classify-intent Every tear on the authority-read surfaces, newest first, each with the instant and event id of the tear, the stack members whose value changed, the stack tuple before and at the tear, and whether an acknowledgement covers it. Beside them the acknowledgement log, also newest first, and the granularity a new acknowledgement would take now. surfaceId narrows the read.

POST /lens/authority/tear/acknowledge { "surfaceId": "classify-intent", "approverId": "ops.rivera", "tearEventId": "evt_01H...", "note": "same family, re-validated against the fixture set" } 201 with the minted event id and the record. Omit tearEventId and the lens picks for you: the surface’s latest unacknowledged tear under watermark , its oldest under per-tear . A surface with no gated decision in the current contract is not an authority-read surface, and acknowledging on it is a 404 rather than a silent no-op. So is naming an event that is not a tear. Retries and duplicates The acknowledgement’s event id is derived from the surface and the tear, so resubmitting the same acknowledgement is a keep-first no-op in the store. Acknowledging a tear that is already covered is a 409 , and under per-tear , acknowledging out of order is a 409 that names the older open tear.

Granularity One acknowledgement covers watermark The acknowledged tear and every earlier tear on the surface, in one log record. The default. per-tear Only the acknowledged tear, one log record each, applied oldest first. PUT /lens/authority/policy { "policy": { "tearAckGranularity": "per-tear" }, "approverId": "ops.rivera", "basePolicyId": "ap-9c21f0b47de3a815", "note": "audit asked for one record per tear" } basePolicyId is the record the operator reviewed, and null when the policy in force came from the file seed or the defaults. The schema is strict: an unknown key is refused rather than ignored, so a typo cannot read as a policy that does not apply. Compare-and-swap on the write If the policy moved since the operator reviewed it, the write is refused with authority_policy_conflict rather than overwriting someone else’s change. Reload, re-review, re-submit. The retention policy works the same way. GET /lens/authority/policy returns the policy in force, its source, the operator record behind it or null , whether this backend can write one at all, and whether a configured file seed is being ignored because an operator policy exists. Resolution order is the operator’s persisted policy, then the file seed, then the defaults. A backend that keeps no durable authority-policy store answers the PUT with 501 and reports that in writable . The filesystem backend keeps one. There the policy in force is the file seed at APERTURE_AUTHORITY_POLICY_PATH , or the defaults.

The authority-policy desk in Curate holds the editor, the diff against the policy in force, and the history. The tears card in the Lens Health panel holds the open tears and the acknowledgement. Both go through the same gate as the API, and the desk is read-only on a backend that cannot persist a policy. See The dashboard .

acknowledged on a tear is derived rather than stored: true when a watermark acknowledgement at or after it exists on the surface, or a per-tear acknowledgement of exactly it. The log sits beside the tears rather than inside them, so who released what, when, under which mode, and with what note is readable on its own. Each record keeps the granularity in force when it was made. Changing the mode changes what the next acknowledgement covers and never reinterprets a past one. Acknowledgements are appended as analysis.authority-tear-acknowledged events: server-stamped, append-only, and exempt from compaction. The history behind the policy is append-only too, each record naming the policy it replaced, the operator who approved it, and when.

Method & path Purpose GET /lens/authority/tears The open and covered tears on each surface, the acknowledgement log, and the granularity in force. POST /lens/authority/tear/acknowledge Release one tear. Gated by authority.acknowledge-tear . Body: surfaceId , approverId , optional tearEventId and note . GET /lens/authority/policy The policy in force, its source, the operator record, writable , and seedIgnored . PUT /lens/authority/policy Replace it. Gated by authority.policy , compare-and-swap on basePolicyId . 501 without a durable policy store. GET /lens/authority/policy/history Every operator policy that has been in force, oldest first.

Code Status Meaning authority_tear_already_acknowledged 409 An acknowledgement at or after this tear exists on the surface. authority_tear_ack_out_of_order 409 Under per-tear , an older tear on the surface is still open. The error names it. authority_policy_conflict 409 The policy changed since the operator reviewed it.

Authority is the reading: the six states, the stack, and what withdraws a grant. This chapter is the disposition over it. The gate and its action vocabulary are shared with the retention desk in Compaction & husking and the multiplex run in The multiplexer , which is why the table above reaches past authority. The state ontology, the record shapes, the policy schema and the action identifiers are public contract. Which spans a released window then covers, and how the states are derived from it, lives in the lens.

records.h: Route a verdict to a human
records.t: Chapter 24 Route a verdict to a human The analysis chapters are detection : the lens reads what happened and forms a verdict. This chapter is the layer after it: defense . When a deterministic predicate over the lens's own verdicts fires, the lens POSTs an HMAC-signed webhook to a consumer you control: a pager, a chat channel, or an agent that picks up the work. It speaks only when something crosses a line. There are no "all quiet" pings. Where this sits The webhook is a trigger , not a conclusion. The usual path is: a predicate fires → a human is alerted → the human asks a coding agent to act → and the agent, before it changes anything, consults the reliability and drift reads (see Verdict reliability and Drift attribution ) to decide whether the alert reflects real, trustworthy movement. The alert says what crossed a line; the reads say whether it is safe to act on.

You register a subscription : a predicate to watch, a window, and a webhook to call. On a schedule you own (Cloud Scheduler is the intended trigger), the lens evaluates every subscription against recent verdicts, fires the ones whose predicate matched, and dedupes a repeat of the same finding inside the window. The webhook secret proves the call came from your lens and nobody else.

Writes are approver-gated. The webhook url must be https , and the secret is 16–512 characters. The body is strict: an unknown field is rejected. POST /lens/subscriptions Authorization: Bearer <token> Content-Type: application/json { "predicate": { "kind": "conformance-fail", "surfaceId": "support.triage" }, "windowMs": 300000, "webhook": { "url": "https://alerts.example.com/holonograph", "secret": "<16-512 random chars, kept secret>" }, "approverId": "brian" } Success returns 201 with a redacted view of the subscription: id , agentId , the predicate and window, createdAt / createdBy , and webhook: { url } . The secret is write-only and is never read back . Set it once at create; if you lose it, delete and recreate.

A predicate is a discriminated union on kind . Each names a meaning , never an opaque number. Three ship today: kind Shape Fires when conformance-fail { surfaceId, fixtureId? } A conformance fixture FAILs on the surface (e.g. a required tool was never called). Omit fixtureId to fire on any fixture failure. emission-breach { surfaceId, columnId? } A substrate column declared always-emitted went silent in the window: a deployment is broken, not just underperforming. dimension-below { surfaceId, dimensionId, threshold } A judge dimension scored strictly below threshold in the window. The one predicate that reads a graded score.

Reads are also served under the /holonograph alias. Every read redacts the webhook secret. Method & path Returns GET /lens/subscriptions All subscriptions (optional ?surfaceId= filter), each with webhook: { url } only. GET /lens/subscriptions/:id One subscription, or 404 . DELETE /lens/subscriptions/:id?approverId=<id> Deletes it. approverId is a required query param. Returns { deleted: true, id } . Every read returns the same projection: Field Shape What it tells you id string Server-minted. The handle for read and delete. agentId string Derived from the contract at create time. predicate object The predicate as registered. windowMs number The dedupe window. webhook { url } URL only. The signing secret is write-only. createdAt ISO 8601 When it was registered. createdBy string The approver identity that created it. disabled boolean (opt) Paused: retained but never fires. Absent means enabled. No endpoint sets it on this release, so in practice a read returns it absent. lastFiredAt ISO 8601 (opt) When it last fired. Absent until the first fire. lastFiredFingerprint string (opt) The fingerprint of the last-fired match: the dedupe key the window is measured against. Compare it with the fingerprint on a webhook body to see whether an alert you received was the one that reset the window. There is no update Subscriptions are create / read / delete. To change a predicate, window, or webhook, delete and recreate . There is no edit or pause endpoint on this release.

When a subscription fires, the lens POSTs this body to your url : POST https://alerts.example.com/holonograph x-holonograph-signature: sha256=<hex> Content-Type: application/json { "subscriptionId": "sub_01H...", "agentId": "rupert-swarm", "predicate": { "kind": "conformance-fail", "surfaceId": "support.triage" }, "verdict": { /* structured, per predicate kind: the deterministic detail */ }, "summary": "save_report was never called on support.triage", "fingerprint": "conformance:support.triage:...", "firedAt": "2026-08-22T14:03:11Z" } verdict is a structured object, not a string: it carries the per-kind detail (the failing fixture and violating event ids, the silent column ids, or the dimension, threshold, and below-threshold event ids). summary is the one-line human sentence. fingerprint is the dedupe key.

The x-holonograph-signature header is sha256= followed by the HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body , keyed by the subscription's secret. Verify it over the raw bytes you received , before parsing JSON, and reject anything that does not match. This is the whole reason the secret exists. import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto"; function verifyHolonographWebhook(rawBody, signatureHeader, secret) { const expected = "sha256=" + createHmac("sha256", secret).update(rawBody).digest("hex"); const got = Buffer.from(signatureHeader ?? ""); const want = Buffer.from(expected); // constant-time compare; length-guard first so timingSafeEqual never throws return got.length === want.length && timingSafeEqual(got, want); }

Delivery is deny-by-default . A webhook fires only to a host on the operator's allow-list; with no allow-list, nothing fires . Point the lens at the file with APERTURE_WEBHOOK_ALLOWLIST_PATH . Keep it alongside your judge rubrics. It is a JSON array of hostnames: // $APERTURE_WEBHOOK_ALLOWLIST_PATH [ "alerts.example.com", "localhost" ] Rule Behavior Deny-by-default No allow-list (absent, empty, or malformed) ⇒ every host is denied and nothing fires. Exact hostname Case-insensitive exact match. No wildcards or suffixes : *.example.com is not a thing; list each host. https required https for every remote host. http is tolerated only for loopback ( localhost , 127.0.0.1 , ::1 ) for local development. No internal targets At fire time the lens pins the resolved address and refuses private, loopback, link-local (incl. the cloud metadata address), and CGNAT ranges. It does not follow redirects. A demo or local bundle ships an allow-list with localhost in it so webhooks fire against a dev consumer.

Nothing fires on its own. Point Cloud Scheduler (bearer-gated) at the evaluate endpoint on the cadence you want; each call is one evaluation cycle across all subscriptions. POST /lens/subscriptions/evaluate Authorization: Bearer <scheduler-token> The response is counts only : the silence discipline again; there is no per-subscription "all quiet": { "evaluated": 12, "matched": 3, "fired": 2, "deduped": 1, "blocked": 0, "skipped": 0, "capped": 0, "allowlistConfigured": true, "errors": [] } A match whose fingerprint already fired within its windowMs is suppressed ( deduped ), so one broken deployment is one alert, not a storm. Dedupe state is stamped only on a successful delivery, so a blocked or failed send re-attempts next cycle. Each cycle fires at most 100 webhooks; matches past that are capped and re-attempted next cycle.

Method & path Purpose POST /lens/subscriptions Create a subscription (approver-gated). GET /lens/subscriptions · GET /holonograph/subscriptions List (secret redacted). Optional ?surfaceId= . GET /lens/subscriptions/:id · GET /holonograph/subscriptions/:id Read one (secret redacted). DELETE /lens/subscriptions/:id?approverId= Delete (approver-gated). POST /lens/subscriptions/evaluate Run one evaluation cycle (Cloud Scheduler; bearer-gated).

The wire types live in @holonograph/types-public : CreateSubscriptionRequest , SubscriptionView , SubscriptionPredicate , SubscriptionWebhookPayload , and EvaluateSubscriptionsResponse . There is no subscriptions helper in @holonograph/client ; build the requests against the types and call the endpoints over HTTP. Honest-null when unwired On a pure-collector lens with no subscription store configured, every route above answers 501 rather than appearing configured. The Defense layer is present only where an operator has wired it.

Chapter 25 Outcome delivery The trip this chapter is about is the outcome’s trip to the user, after scoring, not the event’s trip into the lens. A surface can be green on quality and still never reach anyone, and the two facts are measured separately. The feature is called declare-your-reach, and its discipline is that the lens reports delivery only as far as it can observe it.

The contract declares the post-outcome stages an outcome traverses between the lens’s scoring point and the user. Stages fan in across surfaces, so each is declared once at the contract root and referenced by the surfaces that route through it. { "postOutcomeStages": { "digest-batch": { "kind": "deferred-delivery", "observability": "declared" }, "policy-filter": { "kind": "filter", "observability": "declared" }, "inbox": { "kind": "other", "observability": "reconciled", "settleMs": 3600000 } }, "surfaces": [ { "surfaceId": "draft-reply", "postOutcomeStages": ["digest-batch", "policy-filter", "inbox"] } ] } A surface with no postOutcomeStages makes no delivery claim, and the lens says nothing about its reach. A reference that does not resolve in the map is ignored by the reach reader rather than failing registration, which keeps a stale ref from taking down a contract. Kind What it does to an outcome deferred-delivery Held for a schedule or batch window, delivered later. filter May suppress it. A rule can drop it before the user. cache Served from or written to a cache layer. rate-limit Throttled. May coalesce or shed under load. fan-in Merges outcomes from several surfaces into one delivery. other Declared and uncategorized. filter is the only kind that can suppress an outcome. The rest delay it. The distinction changes what a verdict on the surface is worth, which is why the kind is declared rather than inferred. Each stage also declares whether the lens can see traversal. declared means the operator is telling the lens the stage exists while it emits nothing: the lens cannot verify delivery through it, so every verdict on that surface covers scoring only, and the read reports that. reconciled means the stage emits a footprint per outcome, so the lens observes traversa …

A verdict is a claim about what the agent produced. Treating it as a claim about what the user received is the substitution this chapter exists to block. On a surface with a declared filter downstream, a clean verdict and a user who never saw the output are fully compatible, and nothing in the scoring record would show it. So the attention spine carries both halves of the finding under one source, reach-gap , with different weight. The horizon variant is a declared scope limit rather than a detected failure, so it rides the quiet coverage band. The shortfall variant is a detected failure, with severity scaled to the observed dark rate.

POST /lens/reach/footprint { "correlationId": "corr_01H...", "surfaceId": "draft-reply", "stageId": "inbox", "occurredAt": "2026-11-06T18:22:14.812Z" } One observation: the outcome for this correlation id was seen reaching this stage at this time. Nothing about whether that was good. 202 with the count accepted, and the body also takes { "footprints": [ ... ] } for the high-volume path. The store dedups by correlation id and stage, keep-first, so retries are safe. The strongest footprint is the user’s own return, a reply or a read receipt, emitted on the terminal stage. Without a footprint store wired, or without a contract registry to scope the write, the endpoint answers 501 .

GET /lens/reach?surfaceId=draft-reply&since=2026-10-01T00:00:00Z One entry per surface that declares stages. Surfaces that make no claim are omitted rather than reported empty. Each entry names the terminal stage and its kind, and classifies the read: State Meaning Report measured The terminal stage is reconciled and outcomes have settled. Present. horizon The terminal stage is declared . The lens is told it exists and cannot observe it. null . No rate is derived. no-outcomes Reconciled, but nothing was scored on the surface in the window. null . Omitting since applies the operator’s default read window, echoed back as readWindow so the denominator is never implicit.

Disposition Derived from in-flight Scored, no terminal footprint, still within the settle window. An honest unknown. delivered A footprint at the terminal reconciled stage. dark Past the settle window with no terminal footprint. Observed absence. superseded A newer outcome for the same target replaced it. expired A declared freshness deadline passed before delivery. The first three are derived today. The last two are declared in the enum so the vocabulary is whole and the fuller model arrives without a wire change. settleMs on the terminal stage sets the boundary between in-flight and dark ; absent, the reader’s default applies.

darkRate is dark / settled , where settled is delivered + dark . In-flight outcomes are excluded from both sides, so an outcome whose fate is still unknown is never counted as either. With nothing settled the rate is null rather than zero. byLastStage groups the dark outcomes by the furthest stage a footprint was seen at, which is the useful read: where they stopped. A stageId of null means the outcome was never seen past scoring. medianDarkAgeMs says how old the dark ones are, which separates a broken stage from a slow one. The reach-gap exemplar in the spine carries the declared topology in order, each stage with its kind and observability, the scored-outcome count as the denominator, and a flag when a suppressing stage sits among the unobserved ones. For the horizon variant the sample list is empty by construction: the proof is the declaration, not a representative call. Where footprints live The footprint store is append-only and separate from the canonical event store, and it is never an input to the lens hash. Footprints are transient observations, so a backend may fold settled outcomes into per-surface, per-day tallies and prune past the rate window. The derived rate is what persists. Growth is bounded by the in-flight outcomes plus surfaces times days in window, never by every footprint ever emitted.

Method & path Purpose GET /lens/reach The per-surface delivery read: measured rate, or an honest horizon . Takes surfaceId , since , until . Re-derived per read. POST /lens/reach/footprint Emit one observed footprint or a batch. Idempotent. 202 with the count accepted.

Field Where Meaning postOutcomeStages Contract root The stage topology, keyed by stage id. postOutcomeStages Surface The stage ids this surface routes through, in order. kind Stage One of the six kinds. Drives how the reach caveat is phrased. observability Stage declared or reconciled . Defaults to declared . settleMs Stage How long after scoring a footprint is still awaited. Meaningful on a reconciled terminal stage. description Stage Optional operator note, carried into the drill.

Sidecar / OTel integration covers the other direction: the event’s trip into the lens, and what happens when a drain channel is unreachable. The attention spine carries the reach-gap source and its two bands. The Trust tab in The dashboard renders this read beside rubric coverage, since both answer whether a green verdict can be believed. The stage vocabulary, the disposition enum, the footprint shape and the report shape are public contract. The pairing, the disposition derivation and the rate aggregation live in the lens.
Chapter 26 Compaction & husking Compaction removes the bulky payload from an aging event and keeps every structured field any estimator reads. The lens never compacts on its own.

An operator-invoked pipeline: plan, verify, seal, move. Three endpoints, and the first of them writes nothing. Endpoint Behavior POST /lens/retention/plan Always a dry run. Reports what would be compacted and writes nothing. POST /lens/retention/compact Executes an approved plan. Approver-gated. POST /lens/retention/unseal Undoes an archive-mode seal.

Every event kind declares one. The enumeration is exhaustive, so a new event kind fails the type check until it has been classified. Class Meaning never Never compacted. Evidence, markers and seals. husk Payload may be archived or deleted; structured fields are kept. summarise Compactable only into lossless summaries.

Husking keeps every structured field an estimator reads: ids, occurredAt , the whole substrate, the surface grading including dimension scores, judge identity and structured claims, gate outcomes, cohort tags, light identity and accounting. What leaves is bulk: light.rawRequest , rawResponse , reasoning , toolCalls , vendorMetadata , error.message , each dimension's rationale , sideEffects[].details , and oversized unknown keys. Where the payload went is recorded on the husk. archived means a sealed, hash-chained archive segment holds the full event and the operator can unseal it. deleted means it is gone and only the digest remains. erased means a right-to-delete request removed it.

A husk stamp is server-projected. It exists only on husks the compactor wrote into a sealed husk segment, it is never written onto a stored raw event, and every producer ingest path rejects an event that arrives carrying one. A forged stamp would claim facts the lens never extracted.

Some consumers read the payload: verdict reliability, co-groundedness, trajectory, exemplars. The husk carries a facts block holding those extractors' outputs, computed over the raw event at seal time and stamped with each extractor's version. A consumer whose extractor version or configuration no longer matches reports a method boundary rather than a clean result.

Plan first and read the plan. It is a dry run by construction, not by flag. Compact against an approved plan. The approval is the gate. Prefer archive mode where the payload may be wanted again; an archive seal can be unsealed, a delete cannot. Every consumer of event history declares its post-compaction fidelity, so check that declaration before compacting a span an analysis still depends on.

A compacted span reads the same as an uncompacted one for every structured consumer. Scores, grading, gate outcomes and identity are unchanged, because none of them lived in the payload. A reading that cannot be reproduced on a husk says so as a method boundary.

A policy is a standing disposition the operator approved. The lens never adopts one: the store-capacity finding recommends a preset and stops there. Under schedule: manual nothing runs on its own; under schedule: auto each nightly run remains that same approved disposition, and each one mints a seal and a spine entry. Method & path Purpose GET /lens/retention/policy The policy in force, its source ( operator , file or default ), the operator record, whether PUT is available here, and whether a file seed is being ignored. PUT /lens/retention/policy Replace it. Approver-gated, compare-and-swap on basePolicyId , and a delete-mode policy needs an explicit acknowledgement. Appends to the durable history, then mints the audit record. 501 without a policy store. GET /lens/retention/policy/history Every operator policy, oldest first. GET /lens/retention/schedule The schedule and the auto-run log. Reports supported: false where it cannot run. GET /lens/retention/compaction Status: tiers, seals, chain head, any interrupted operation. ?verify=true re-reads every segment and checks the chain. POST /lens/retention/compaction/prepare The one-time index preparation a backend needs before its first compaction. Approver-gated and explicit; the filesystem backend needs none. A read-window override naming an undeclared surface is a warning The policy schema refuses duplicate or ambiguous read-window overrides and unknown run modes outright. An override naming a surface the contract does not declare is accepted instead, with a warnings entry: the contract may be about to declare it, and refusing would make policy and contract impossible to deploy in either order.

Sealed segments can be mounted back for reading, and data can be removed on request. Every write here is approver-gated, because the lens rehydrates and erases on no one's initiative but the operator's. Method & path Purpose GET /lens/archive/overlays The mounted rehydrate overlays. Also reported on health. POST /lens/archive/rehydrate Mount archive segments as a read-only overlay with a TTL, selected by segmentIds , window or decompositionEventId . Verifies the chain and footer digests and decrypts where needed. Nothing is appended. POST /lens/archive/unmount End an overlay before its TTL. POST /lens/archive/erase/plan A dry run of a right-to-delete erasure: the members by tier, the seals it re-segments, the segments it shreds, the frozen windows it touches, what is removed and what survives. Writes nothing. POST /lens/archive/erase Execute a reviewed plan. Approver-gated and requires acknowledgeIrreversible: true ; the server re-plans and refuses a plan that has moved. An overlay is read-only and expires. Rehydrating does not reverse a compaction: it makes a sealed span readable for as long as the TTL lasts, and appends nothing. A backend without the archive surface answers the read with { supported: false, reason } and every write with 501 , rather than an empty success.

On Firestore, compaction is opt-in and never edits a record in order to build its index. The judge-verdict linking model is husk-invariant: a husked event resolves the same verdict a whole one does. Retention policy and schedule are stored durably and are operator-owned.

Chapter 27 The dashboard An operator interface ships in the binary. It is a thin client over the reads in the rest of this Guide: every number on it comes from a documented endpoint, so this chapter is an index from the panel you are looking at to the chapter that explains it, not a second account of the instrument.

The server mounts it when asked, at /dashboard or a configured base path. With it mounted, a request to / redirects there, so an operator who browses the server’s URL with no path lands on the interface instead of an error about the run mode. The bundle is served ahead of the authenticated router, so its HTML, JS and CSS load without a bearer token. Every /lens/* fetch the page then makes goes through the same auth as any other client. Optional HTTP Basic credentials gate the bundle path itself, which a production deploy should set; local development usually leaves it unset. What each credential gates Basic auth on the dashboard path gates the UI bundle and nothing else. The bearer token in the settings dialog is what reads the lens. Setting the first does not protect the API, and setting the second does not hide the page. Settings holds three things: the lens endpoint, the bearer token, and whether to poll. They persist in the browser. Three URL parameters change the mode without being saved: ?mock=true renders canned data for a demo, ?embed=1 hides the operator chrome for an iframed lens and defaults the palette to dark, and ?theme=light or dark pins the palette for that load only. The header carries a version chip. It shows the active contract version when one is registered, and falls back to the binary’s own stamp, labelled as such, when none is.

The interface is organized by the four questions an operator actually arrives with, not by the shape of the API. Each tab owns one, and the deeper instruments open over the tab that owns them, so a ceremony has one home. Nothing on it writes the lens. The exceptions are the gated ceremonies, and each goes through the one shared approver gate described in Authority governance : a triage annotation, a conformance approval, a retention or authority policy, a multiplex run. The apparatus proposes and the operator disposes, on the interface exactly as on the API.

Tab The question Reads Act What needs attention now. GET /lens/attention , GET /lens/attention/evidence , POST /lens/attention/triage Trust Can I believe the numbers, and where am I blind. GET /lens/reach , GET /lens/facet-coverage , GET /lens/judge-claim-coverage , POST /lens/co-groundedness/screen Curate What change should I propose and approve. GET /aperture/contract , GET /lens/facet-coverage , plus the desk cards below Explore What do the raw events say. GET /lens/events , GET /lens/events/{id} , GET /aperture/contract , GET /lens/availability Act is the landing. It is one severity-ranked queue over every finding source, with the jargon moved into the drawer: a row reads “Judge check,” opens into the driver and the sample calls, and takes a disposition with a required rationale. A confirmed defect mints a proposal into Curate. Trust is the standing-health counterpart: the readouts you check before believing a clean verdict. Explore is the bench the other three route down into, scoped by whatever row sent you there.

Fourteen instruments open over a tab rather than competing with it for a tab of their own. Panel Reads Chapter Lens Health #lens-health /aperture/contract , /lens/topology/scan , /lens/events , /lens/snapshots Topology scanner Lens Health operations /aperture/health , /lens/availability , /lens/authority/tears , /lens/attribute Authority governance Multiplexer /lens/events , POST /lens/multiplex/run (gated) Multiplexer Eval workbench /lens/events , POST /lens/decomposition/evaluate , POST /lens/decomposition/lifecycle Variance isolation Lessons pipeline /aperture/contract , /lens/events Lessons pipeline Conformance authoring POST /lens/conformance/derive , /lens/conformance/check , /lens/conformance/fixtures Conformance Judge transfer curve /lens/events below Verdict reliability /lens/verdict-reliability SDK reference Trajectory /lens/trajectory-findings Attention spine Seam-soak monitor #seam-soak /lens/attention?surfaceId=system.seam-soak Seam monitor Builder-seam monitor #builder-seam /lens/attention?surfaceId=system.builder-seam Seam monitor Seam to call analysis #seam-call-analysis /lens/seam-call-analysis Seam monitor Retention desk #curate?desk=retention /lens/retention/policy , /plan , /compact , /unseal , /schedule , the archive routes Compaction Authority policy desk /lens/authority/policy , /policy/history , PUT /lens/authority/policy Authority governance The three monitors are deliberately outside the Act queue. A seam backlog is a coverage list to work through, not a firefighting queue, and the evidence rides inline on each item, so opening one costs a single read.

One panel has no endpoint of its own. It asks whether a surface’s judge is a graded transfer function or a step function, and it answers from the score distribution the lens already captured, with no new calls to the judge. Characterization What a bad reading looks like Quantization A handful of distinct scores over a decent sample. The judge is stepping, not grading. Dead zones Large gaps between consecutive achieved scores. Ranges the judge never lands in. Concentration The most common score holds most of the mass. Barely discriminating. Saturation Events piled at the low or high end of the observed range. What it cannot see is stated on the panel: the perturbation-response cliffs. Finding those means feeding the judge altered inputs, which is a live call rather than an observation, and outside what the lens does. The distribution behind the characterization is in GET /lens/events , and the adjacent question of whether a rubric still discriminates at all is the saturation audit in Rubric coverage and de-saturation .

The hash is a route and carries a query string, so a finding, a facet or a desk can be linked directly. An unrecognized tab name falls back to Act. Link Opens #act?severity=&state=&surface=&source= The queue, filtered. #explore?surface=&facet=&dimension= The rubric drill for one facet. #explore?event= One event. #curate?desk=retention&preset= The retention desk, preset applied. #lens-health · #seam-soak · #builder-seam · #seam-call-analysis The named monitor, over the tab beneath it.

Where a read is an honest null, the panel says which null it is rather than rendering a zero. Trust shows horizon on a surface whose delivery the lens cannot observe, instead of a reach rate. Trajectory puts its unmeasured accounting first, so events with no boundary key are never read as clean. Verdict reliability shows its review tier separately, labelled as no deterministic check applied, which is not the same as a pass. The same discipline governs the version chip: with no contract registered it reports binary rather than a contract version it does not have.

Route Behavior GET /dashboard The bundle. Served ahead of auth; optional HTTP Basic gates this path only. GET / A 302 to the dashboard when it is mounted. Unprotected, so the browser follows it into the credential prompt. GET /lens/version The header chip’s read: the active contract version, or the binary stamp.

Every panel above is a rendering, and the chapter column is where the measurement itself is explained. Two ceremonies on the interface are the only writes an operator makes often: the triage disposition in Act, covered in The attention spine , and the policy desks, covered in Authority governance and Compaction & husking . The interface ships with the binary and tracks it. Where this chapter and a panel disagree, the panel is newer.
